description: Focus-dependent historical benchmarks for game years 600-1200 (about 1500 BCE to 360 CE: the late palace states, the post-collapse village world, the classical city-states and the large territorial states). A society that pours itself into one research line or a mixed archetype is judged against what comparable societies achieved with that emphasis: higher bands on its focus metrics, lower bands elsewhere, and at least one required cost below the base typical. Human summary and calibration notes: docs/research/BENCHMARKS_FOCUS_1200.md. Resolver and validator: tools/research/focus_bench.py.

position_scale.meaning: a band position on the base band's own scale, oriented so larger is better ('neither' metrics: numerically larger)

anchors.-2: worse plausibility bound (min; max for 'lower' metrics)
anchors.2: better plausibility bound (max; min for 'lower' metrics)

position_scale.interpolation: linear between anchors, geometric for metrics listed as 'log' in metric_scales; positions interpolate linearly between years
position_scale.modifier: [low_pos, typical_pos, high_pos]; min and max never move; an omitted metric is neutral [-1, 0, 1]
position_scale.construction: from each focus metric's signed design strength s (x era_weight): boost -> [-1 + 0.15 s, 0.5 s, min(1 + 0.25 s, 1.5)]; cost a = |s| -> [-1 - 0.15 a, -0.4 a, 1 - 0.35 a]. Shifted ('neither') metrics use the same formulas with up = +. Year 600 is the join: focus_bench.py judges year 600 with the 0-600 file, so this file's 600 row copies that file's 600 positions (neutral where it has none) and the band is continuous; this window's profile takes over by 700. Metrics marked carried_from_600 are 0-600 effects that fade to neutral by 700. Required costs therefore apply from 700.

era_weight_doc: Line focuses and the five generic archetypes apply at full strength throughout: a focus held since before 600 is already at full effect at the join. The era archetypes follow the time such societies existed: palace and temple economies are strongest at 600 and weakened by the collapse around 700; citizen militias peak 800-900; steppe-edge cavalry powers mature from 800; territorial empires from 1000.

roles.boost: focus metric: effective typical above the base typical; may pass the effective high by allowed_lead.per_metric (else .boosted) x |high - typical|
roles.cost: effective typical below the base typical; no lead past the (lowered) high
roles.shift: 'neither' metric moved up or down (e.g. more people under arms); must stay inside the shifted low..high
roles.context: largest_settlement_historical and major_innovations_per_century describe the whole era's record, not the player's society; this window's profiles never modify them (0-600 effects on them fade out by 700)

shock_hazard_mult_doc: Per focus, optional multipliers on benchmarks_1200.json shock_widening.hazard_per_game_century: connected trade societies and empires suffer more pandemics, redistributive palace economies more systemic collapse, stewards fewer famines.

classification.rule: share = emphasis units on a line / all units (the research_emphasis order). 1) An archetype matches when its lines hold >= 55% combined, >= 12% each, and no line holds >= 40%; the best combined share wins. 2) Otherwise every line with share >= 25% gets weight min(1, (share - 1/12) / (0.40 - 1/12)); any remaining weight goes to 'balanced'; weights are normalised and the focus is that blend. 3) Nothing >= 25%: balanced. A line focus's labor/decree 'signature' adds 0.15 to its line's share. Timed strategies are classified per phase. Same thresholds as the 0-600 file.

surrogate_proxies._doc: Metrics without a probe_key have no absolute surrogate measure; these facets stand in for them in the relative (same-seed balanced) checks.
defense_labor_share: defense_share (surrogate row field, not yet a facet)
